answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring hardware-rooted identity: each agent runs inside a trusted execution enclave that signs a unique attestation key, like copper traces etched once per chip — one chip, one identity. A ridge of verification servers checks the attestation before the agent can trade, and a velvet-rope onboarding queue rate-limits new enrollments to a few hundred a day. Faking a thousand agents means buying a thousand real chips, roughly $50,000 in hardware, while honest agents enroll free.
